articleTitle: Research on battery SOH estimation method based on electrochemical impedance spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are widely used in electric vehicles, energy storage systems and portable electronic devices due to their high energy density, high power density and long service life. Battery state-of-health (SOH) has become a focus of current research due to the difficulty of accurately obtaining it in real time. Most of the existing SOH estimation methods are unable to establish the intrinsic connection between their intrinsic aging mechanisms, thus affecting the SOH estimation accuracy. In this paper, a method for SOH estimation of battery based on electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is proposed. Firstly, the relationship between EIS, state of charge (SOC) and SOH is discussed through experimental analysis, and 7 feature factors were selected to characterize the aging state of the battery. Then, the extreme learning machine algorithm is used to train the network with selected feature factors to achieve SOH estimation. Finally, an experimental platform is set up to verify the proposed method. The results show that the maximum relative error of SOH estimation is 2.06%, and the maximum relative error of another battery in the same batch is 2.23%.

articleTitle: Planning for electric-vehicle evacuations: energy, infrastructure, and storage needs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: As we advance toward an era of high electric vehicle (EV) adoption, it is critical to address the power requirements for EVs during disaster evacuations, particularly in scenarios of grid failure. This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the energy needs of EVs during evacuations using a pragmatic stochastic methodology that is both user-friendly and computationally efficient compared to traditional optimization tools. The study evaluates the power requirements of charging infrastructure for various evacuation scenarios, and benchmarks them against the existing infrastructure in several California cities. Additionally, the paper examines the necessary size of backup lithium battery storage to ensure EVs can be adequately powered during evacuations in the absence of grid support. This research offers valuable insights for emergency planners and policymakers to enhance evacuation readiness in the context of increasing EV penetration.

articleTitle: A Generic Approach to Extracting Maximum Power from PMSG Wind Turbines without Current Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Power grids have encountered significant integration of wind energy conversion systems (WECSs) in recent years, aiming at carbon neutrality and net zero emissions. This will result in more complex control of power systems due to the intermittent operation of WECSs. This study explores a more streamlined approach to the maximum power extraction (MPE) technique, aiming to preserve the advantages of conventional MPE while substantially simplifying the control system. The novelty of the proposed method is to develop machine equations incorporating wind speed and potential disturbances and effectively manage voltages and currents to optimize the wind turbine’s performance. Additionally, this approach eliminates current and voltage measurements as well as the need for complicated tuning processes. Various comprehensive experimental analyses are performed to meticulously assess the performance of the proposed method. These results are then compared with the field-oriented control method.

articleTitle: The effect of increasing the thermal conductivity of a cylindrical cell housing on thermal performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The development and utilization of larger format cylindrical cells has become more prevalent in industry with a key consideration being thermal management. This paper aims to identify the effect of increasing the thermal conductivity of the cell housing on the heat rejection and thermal performance of a 4680 cell under both side and base cooling schemes with significant reduction in both maximum temperature and thermal gradients seen. It is also shown that by using the modified housing with thermal conductivity k=250 W/mK, cold plate size may be reduced by over 50% whilst maintaining the thermal performance of the standard cell.

articleTitle: Asymmetric Supply of a Dual Three-Phase PMSM through a Hybrid Energy Storage System in Marine Electric Propulsion Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel electric propulsion system architecture for marine applications. This consists of a Hybrid Energy Storage System (HESS) supplying a Dual Three-Phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine (DTP-PMSM), which is connected to a marine propeller through a gearbox so that it acts as the propulsion motor of the vessel. The HESS is made up of a battery pack and a supercapacitor module, each of which supplies one of the two DTP-PMSM three-phase windings through suitable DC/DC and DC/AC converters. Vessel speed can be regulated through suitable DTP-PMSM speed and current control loops. Additionally, torque/power demand can be split asymmetrically between the two DTP-PMSM windings according to power and/or energy capability of each HESS unit. The proposed configuration is validated through numerical simulations, which highlight the effectiveness of both HESS energy management and DTP-PMSM control systems.

articleTitle: Enhanced Energy Management using Powertrain and Mission parameters : Case study of a Distributed Hybrid Propulsion Light Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Nowadays, the aeronautical field is transitioning from conventional fuel to electricity or hydrogen energy vectors. New environmental regulations constraining aircraft manufacturers push them towards new aircraft and powertrain architectures. These architectures largely differ from the current ones and require new design standards. All of the aircraft design stages are concerned. The research work presented in this article stems from a need of defining the influence of the Energy Management System on the early design stages. Previous work laid down the design basis. This paper showcases an energy management strategy associating powertrain and aircraft operation. Results over 5 flights highlight significant fuel savings as well as design discrepancies.

articleTitle: Parameter Estimation for a Generic Na-ion Battery Model Using The Curve Fitting Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper presents two models for a new sodiumion battery based technology, validated using dynamic driving profiles (Artemis and WLTC). Initially, a simplified model with only a series resistor is presented. Although this model closely followed the experimental curve, it failed to capture the system’s high dynamics. Then, an enhanced model with a parallel RC circuit is presented. This addition significantly improved the model’s ability to capture the dynamic behavior of the battery under varying current inputs, closely matching the experimental data. The parameters for the models were determined with curve fitting using Matlab’s optimization toolbox. The comparative analysis revealed that while the simplified series resistor model provided a basic approximation, the RC model offered superior accuracy, particularly in scenarios involving rapid current changes.

articleTitle: Real Time Adaptive Energy Management Strategy for Electric Vehicles with Hybrid Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: In recent years, the mobility sector has experienced many radical innovations, including the widespread adoption of hybrid and fully electric road vehicles. Notably, the possibility of fitting multiple types of energy storage devices in road vehicles has garnered significant interest from researchers, industrial partners, and governments. This paper proposes an innovative energy management strategy for a hybrid battery-supercapacitor fully electric race car, designed for the IEEE Vehicular Technology Society Motor Vehicle Challenge 2024. The proposed solution focuses on optimizing the management of the vehicle energy storage systems to minimize the losses of the power converters and the electric motor.

articleTitle: Systematic Modeling of a Steering Vehicle Differential Using Power-Oriented Graphs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper concerns the systematic modeling of a steering vehicle differential using power-oriented graphs. The proposed modeling provides two power-oriented block schemes: a full elastic one and a reduced-order rigid one, both allowing to effectively simulate the considered differential equipped with clutches. The proposed modeling procedure is fully systematic, following a step-by-step process and employing two algorithms for the calculation of the model matrices. The considered simulation scenario, which includes the locking and unlocking phases of the differential clutches, shows the good superposition between the results given by the full and reduced-order models.

articleTitle: Active Suppression of Low-Order Current Harmonics for 400kW Dual Three-Phase IPMSM Drives in Heavy-Duty EV Traction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Dual three-phase interior permanent magnet synchronous machines (DTP-IPMSMs) are usually driven by voltage source inverters. There are 64 basic voltage vectors which can be used to synthesize reference voltage vectors in the αβ subspace and z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> subspace simultaneously. However, it becomes impossible when the modulation index increases. As a result, the harmonic currents in the z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> subspace will be out of control. Intermediate vectors are introduced to synthesize reference voltage vectors, and the amplitude of intermediate vectors is variable. Then, the harmonic currents could be suppressed. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Design of a 1200Nm High Torque Density In-Wheel Magnetic Geared Motor for Electrical Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: In the emerging field of electric vehicle technology, research on in-wheel motors has received increasing attention due to its ability to control independent wheels and direct drive, thereby improving operational flexibility. Due to the limited space and weight within the wheel, the size of the motor is reduced, which affects the output torque of the motor, thus limiting the performance of traditional permanent magnet motors. The magnetic geared motor is suitable for the application of in-wheel motors because of its low speed and high torque characteristics. This paper designs a three-airgap in-wheel magnetic geared motor based on a 16-inch wheel. Utilizing the high torque and low-speed characteristics of the magnetic geared motor, it can achieve a maximum output torque of 1202Nm, with a torque volume density of 120Nm/L. Compared to reference direct-drive in-wheel motor, its torque volume density is increased by 78%. and the current density and electrical load are reduced to 4.4 A/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and 450A/cm respectively.

articleTitle: Minimizing the Energy Consumption of BEV Speed Trajectory Based on Dynamic Programming
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Especially, people consider changing the Battery Electric Vehicle because of the air pollution. But the power to move the vehicle is made of the fossil fuel that is influenced by the air pollution. Therefore, optimizing the vehicle movement is necessary. Finding the optimal speed trajectory use Dynamic programming to guarantee the global optimization in certification cycle (UDDS, HWFET cycle). Because the certification cycle exists all the driving scenarios (acceleration, braking, coasting, cruising), Speed trajectory is derived from the various driving scenarios. The speed trajectory has a phenomenon of following the lower boundary, coast driving and using the high motor efficiency.

articleTitle: Integration of the fuel cell degradation in a 0D/1D vehicle system model in GT-SUITE
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Hydrogen fuel cells are a solution to reduce pollutant emissions and greenhouse gases in the automotive industry. Fuel cell modeling is necessary for design, development purposes and achieve the desired levels of durability. Even though a lot of advancement have been made in the electrochemical modeling of fuel cells, improvements need to be made on the degradation models. At Symbio, a degradation model coupled to a well calibrated Butler-Volmer electrochemical model has been developed and tested to assess the impact of fuel cell ageing on its performance. With this model, the fuel cell efficiency loss can be quantified as well as the overconsumption of the system ancillaries.

articleTitle: Impact of Battery Temperature on Charging Time of an Electric Vehicle for Slow Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The performance of electric vehicles is affected by the thermal conditions. This paper studies the influence of ambient temperature on the charging time of electric vehicles (EVs) during slow charging. The accuracy of the studied system model is validated using experimental data from a Nissan Leaf charging session. Energetic Macroscopic Representation (EMR) formalism is used to organize the interconnections of the battery electro-thermal model with a charger system. Simulation results indicate that the charging time of the battery rises to 18 hours at -23°C and 9 hours at -20°C, compared to 7.5 hours at the standard operating temperatures.

articleTitle: Parameter Adaptive Control of the Virtual DC Machine Based on Sigmoid Function
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Due to the lack of inertia and damping in DC microgrids, virtual DC machine (VDCM) control is applied to DC converters to enhance the ability of the bus voltage to suppress fluctuations. However, the conventional VDCM adopts fixed parameters, which makes it more difficult for the system to achieve good dynamic performance while obtaining inertia and damping support. To address this problem, a parameter adaptive control based on the sigmoid function is proposed in this paper. By establishing the connection between the rate of voltage change and the control parameter, an adaptive sigmoid function is designed so that the parameter can be adjusted more smoothly and adaptively in the case of power fluctuations. Simulations and experimental results show that the proposed control achieves smaller voltage drop and shorter recovery time compared with the conventional VDCM control.

articleTitle: The Influence of Overcharging and Over-Discharging on the Capacity Degradation of Lithium-Ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIB) are the best technology for supplying and storing energy for electric mobility systems. Despite that, this technology is sensitive to abuses that can compromise its lifetime and cause fire and explosion risks. In this context, if LIB is not correctly controlled, some abuses, such as overcharging (OC) and over-discharging (OD), can be observed and provoke a loss of capacity. Therefore, this work presented the application of several experiments in cells, of the NMC type, under OC and the combination of OC and OD. The results indicated that cells charged until 4.4 and 4.5 V and discharged until 3.0 V do not lose capacity for twenty-five cycles, but more cycles should be done to understand the impact over time. On the other side, the cell charged until 4.6 and 4.8 V had its security protection romped in the fourth charging cycle, and the cell charged until 5.0 V had its safety compromised in the first charging cycle. Conversely, cells with a combination of OC and OD were more compromised. In this context, while a cell is submitted only with OC and does not lose capacity, a cell under OC and then under OD had its protection romped in the third charging cycle. Cells under 4.6 V and 4.8 V lost capacity during the second charging cycle. In conclusion, OC provokes a high level of degradation in the cell, but the combination of OC and OD causes even more degradation.

articleTitle: Wheel-speed based Driving Force Control for On-board Motor Electric Vehicles with Absolute Stability Analysis and HIL Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Driving force control (DFC) has been well-developed for in-wheel-motor electric vehicles (IWM-EVs). However, due to the powertrain complexity, DFC for on-board motor electric vehicles (OBM-EVs) is still an open challenge, especially in system configuration and stability analysis. To address these issues, this paper proposes (i) a novel cascade two-degree-of-freedom DFC for OBM-EVs and (ii) an absolute stability analysis of the overall system with respect to the maximum allowable wheel speed, which depends on the driving situation. In the outer layer, a feedback-feedforward reaction force controller directly generates the wheel speed references. In the inner layer, a feedback-feedforward speed controller generates the motor torque. By utilizing a real IWM-EV, a hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) system is developed to imitate the OBM-EV properly. HIL results show that the proposed stability analysis can effectively predict the system behavior. The proposed system successfully improves the DFC performances with quick response, less vibration, and accurate tracking.

articleTitle: Current Sensorless Direct Voltage Control of Surface Mounted Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Driven Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Fast and accurate response, quick recovery from various disturbances, simplicity, reliability, and cost-effectiveness are essential features of an efficient motor drive system for electric vehicles (EVs). Thus, this paper introduces a simple current sensorless direct voltage control scheme for a surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor (SPMSM) propelling an EV. The designed method provides a promising alternative to cascaded-based control strategies, such as field-oriented control (FOC), by directly varying the amplitude and angle of the voltage vector while excluding measurements of current and inner regulation loops. Such a methodology drastically reduces the complexity and tuning time of the control system and mitigates the delays resulting from cascaded control schemes. It also ensures better reliability since it does not require current sensors. The performance of the developed strategy is investigated using commonly adopted driving cycles, namely the Federal Test Procedure (FTP75) and the World Harmonized Light Vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP). An intensive comparison against FOC is established based on the driving cycles employed.

articleTitle: Robust Energy and Powertrain Losses Management of a Dual-Sources e-Racing Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The increasing use of electric vehicles (EVs) has been encouraged by many nations globally to address the problems brought on by the energy crisis and global warming. However, there are several disadvantages to EVs such as the limitations of the onboard energy storage. To address this issue, another energy storage system (ESS) with high power density is required to form a hybrid energy storage system (HESS). Besides the topology, the component sizing and energy management strategy (EMS) is important for HESS EV. The Motor Vehicle Challenge (MVC) 2024 challenges the participant to propose the best EMS to minimize the objective function provided. The winner is the lowest objective function value. The simple EMS, Robust Low-Pass Filter (RLPF), which is the combination of LPF, rule-based, and feedback control is proposed for MVC 2024. The reduction of the final score for training and verification is 47.58%, and 61.93%, respectively, compared to the base MVC method.

articleTitle: Super-Twisting Sliding Mode Control of a Fully Active Parallel Topology for Hybrid Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Hybrid electric vehicles powered by Li-ion batteries and supercapacitors have recently been considered a promising solution to enhance battery lifetime and driving range. Integrating Bi-directional DC/DC converters is vital to interface various electrical sources with the DC-bus level. Therefore, ensuring a stable DC-bus voltage under uncertainties and fluctuations of electrical power loads is essential for the reliable operation of the on-boarded electrical sources. This paper proposes a super-twisting sliding mode control technique to regulate the DC-bus voltage and control the electrical currents of battery and supercapacitor sources. An Energetic Macroscopic Representation (EMR) and an Inversion-Based Control (IBC) are adopted as a graphical formalism to represent the system under study and the proposed controller. Furthermore, a stability analysis based on the Lyapunov theorem is conducted to ensure the stability of the proposed controller under the Artemis Urban driving cycle.

articleTitle: Optimizing Interior PMSMs for Energy Efficiency: Simple Dynamic Direct Voltage Control for Electric Vehicle during Standard Driving Cycles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This manuscript details a strategy focused on evaluating the energy efficiency of various electric vehicle driving cycles, utilizing a simple dynamic direct voltage MTPA speed control (S-DDVC) technique for IPMSMs. By identifying a unique motor voltage angle and magnitude combination, the MTPA trajectory can be tracked for each reference speed or torque condition, ensuring minimal current and power consumption while enhancing energy efficiency. This approach improves precision under various driving conditions by considering the motor’s dynamic model. The paper also includes a comparative study between the S-DDVC methodology and the traditional FOC strategy within the context of electric vehicle standard driving cycles. Experimental results and quantitative evaluations demonstrate that the S-DDVC strategy is effective and offers higher efficiency for IPMSM drives, making it a viable alternative to current MTPA methods for modern electric vehicle applications.

articleTitle: Assessing the social acceptance of electric vehicles on a campus of university
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This article investigates, through a survey, the barriers met by a sample of 72 campus users when considering the acquisition of an electric vehicle. The participants were also asked to do a driving test of an electric vehicle. The participants’ perception of the vehicle got assessed before, during and after. Thus, the survey could help identify not only barriers, but also levers for action in encouraging the modal report to an electric car. Results from the first phase showed that 82% of participants would like to acquire an electric vehicle. Yet, among them, 57% stated that they were not in a position to acquire one. Most of them are young people and students. This correlation between the capacity to access and electric vehicle and the age and status is supported by statistical analyses.

articleTitle: Modeling and Control of Multi-phase Motor Fed by Multi-level Inverter for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The automotive industry is undergoing an electrification revolution with the adoption of Electric Vehicles (EVs) worldwide. EVs, powered by electric motors, traction inverters, and rechargeable batteries, offer significant benefits in energy efficiency and emissions reduction. Reliability is crucial in pow-ertrain systems. Multi-phase electric motors are gaining attention for their enhanced performance, fault tolerance, and efficiency. Simultaneously, EVs manufacturers are adopting higher-voltage batteries for reduced current, increased power density, and faster charging. Multi-level inverters, such as the Cascaded H-bridge (CHB) topology, provide higher efficiency and better waveform quality compared to two-level inverters. This paper presents a modelling and control methodology for a Five-phase Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (5P-IPMSM) fed by the Seven-level Cascaded H-bridge (7L-CHB) inverter in a high-power, high-reliability traction system.

articleTitle: Enhanced Efficiency in Electric Vehicle Operation: Easy Dynamic Direct Voltage MTPA Control without Current Sensing for Interior PMSMs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The transportation sector is widely acknowledged for contributing the largest share of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. This study presents a strategy aimed at enhancing energy efficiency in electric vehicles by employing an easy dynamic direct voltage method without current sensing for MTPA speed control of interior PMSMs. The approach involves following the MTPA angle using a distinctive voltage magnitude, eliminating the need for current sensing at any speed in electric vehicles. This results in minimized current and power consumption, ultimately leading to heightened energy efficiency. The accomplishment of these objectives is facilitated by incorporating the motor’s dynamic model, which enhances controller responsiveness, especially during dynamics. The experimental outcomes, along with energy consumption measurements and an energy efficiency analysis, substantiate that the suggested Easy Dynamic Direct Voltage Control (E-DDVC) technique is a promising alternative to current MTPA methodologies in interior-PMSM drives. This strategy demonstrates the ability to maintain high energy efficiency, particularly during dynamic operations.

articleTitle: Techno Economic Study of Second life Batteries for Affordable e-mobility campus
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The TESSA project (Techno Economic Study of Second life batteries for an Affordable e-mobility campus) aims to extend electric vehicle battery lifetime through secondary use in stationary applications before recycling. The approach mitigates the ecological impact of batteries while ensuring economic and operational satisfaction for the vehicle owner. The TESSA project brings together partners from electrical engineering, economics, and social science to address the complex benefits and requirements of electric vehicle batteries.

articleTitle: Basic Study on Wheel Speed Based Driving Force Control for Multi-motor Electric Vehicles with Glocal Stability Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel driving force control (DFC) strategy for electric vehicles driven by multi-motors. The proposed system is designed hierarchically, with driving force control in the outer-layer, and wheel speed control in the inner-layer. Notably, the outer-layer controller directly outputs the wheel speed references. This configuration does not requires the vehicle speed to calculate the wheel speed as the traditional DFC, thereby reducing system complexity. Moreover, this paper shows that the proposed system can be modelled as a multi-agent system with generalized frequency variable and a physical interaction matrix of rank-1. This allows us to guarantee the stability of the total system (global) with respect to the actuator dynamics (local). In particular, this paper establishes a D-stability condition, which is independent of the number of motor actuators. The proposed strategy is applied to range extension control via energy optimization by driving force distribution and control.

articleTitle: Dynamic Bidirectional-Controlled Inverter-Based Grid Optimized by Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Grid-based voltage source inverters frequently utilize the droop control technique combined with inner/outer voltage and current regulation mechanisms to ensure a dependable electricity supply. This study seeks to introduce a Cascade-Forward Neural Network (CFNN) control approach designed to lead inverter-based grids when operating in grid-connected or islanded modes, focusing on improving the transient state performance of the CFNN technique. The suggested approach involves utilizing the inverter in a bidirectional manner, suitable for a diverse array of battery energy storage systems and distributed generation setups. The proposed strategy leverages CFNN to grasp the inverter’s non-linear model, enabling precise monitoring of demand and reference power across various operational scenarios within smart grid applications. Furthermore, the approach redefines the grid control concept, guiding the inverter according to optimal parameters that encompass power demand, reference power, equipment dimensions, and external disturbances. Notably, this method circumvents the need for any manual tuning procedures. Furthermore, incorporating dynamic elements into the approach improves the protection system’s responsiveness. This ensures continuous power supply during faults, enabling a more effective and rapid response, enhancing system resilience, and reducing downtime. This dual advantage of better power supply and heightened protection system sensitivity highlights the proposed method’s significance in fortifying the reliability of power systems.. To assess the efficacy of the suggested CFNN controller, its power tracking, operational capabilities, and dynamic response are assessed via multiple experimental trials employing the hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) approach across various scenarios. The outcomes of these tests are meticulously compared to a well-established conventional strategy, affirming the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Integrating System Modeling with CFD Simulations to Define Design Points for Supercapacitor Module Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This study introduces a method for coupling 1D system modeling with 2D/3D computational fluid dynamics (CFD) component modeling for a super capacitor(SC) module with its results. The method aids in designing a natural/forced cooling system for the module, intended for use in combination with diesel generators and battery systems. The study outlines the module sizing process and focuses on its thermal aspects. Surface response functions are built based on CFD results and coupled with a system model using functional mock-up interface (FMU) modeling within Matlab Simulink. Unverified results of module dimensions and operating points are presented. The study’s outcome is a method for improving system models using 2D/3D CFD analysis, which can be applied not only to super capacitors but also to various novel component designs requiring complex cooling or heating architectures, such as battery modules or inverter modules.

articleTitle: Shock absorbing seats for vehicles with pitch motion from explosive impact
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: In recent years, improvised explosive devices (IEDs) have caused explosion damage to occupants when vehicles are moving on roads in conflict zones. To mitigate IED damage, this paper proposes a seating mechanism that cushions the shock propagated through the vehicle to the occupants. A seesaw-type experiment was conducted using a scaled-down model as an alternative to an explosion experiment. As a result of experiment, the model performed a vertical throw-up motion with rotation. The vertical and horizontal accelerations were absorbed by the seating mechanism. The attenuation rate of the horizontal acceleration increased with a smaller spring constant.

articleTitle: Phase Current Reconstruction of Five Phase Open-Winding Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine Using Single DC Bus Current Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The multi-phase open-winding permanent magnet synchronous motor (OW-PMSM) has the advantages of high bus voltage utilization and good fault-tolerant performance, which are mostly used in ship propulsion equipment. However, the use of multiple current sensors reduces system stability and increases system size. There are few studies on the phase current reconstruction technology of multiphase OW-PMSM. In this paper, a five-phase current reconstruction method using a single current sensor is proposed for five-phase OW-PMSM. On the basis of traditional neighbouring four vectors - space vector pulse width modulation(NFV-SVPWM), base vectors with smaller amplitude is selected to improve the linear reconstruction range. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed method was verified through simulation.

articleTitle: Prediction of Electric Vehicle Charge Profile using Battery Digital Twin
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The transition towards vehicle electrification presents various challenges due to uncertainties in charging behavior and battery aging. This study proposes a method to generate an accurate charge profile with a battery Digital Twin (DT). The method is adaptive, has fast prediction and has low training cost. It is intended towards improving the charge scheduling for fleet operators by providing predictions on grid load and charging time. The method was tested with data from a real case study where, for a charging session, it showed an error of less than 2% for charge time and an improvement of 7% over a standard charge profile.

articleTitle: State of Safety Assessment in Electric Vehicle Battery Packs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Ensuring safety and guiding first responders in risk mitigation decisions necessitates an accurate evaluation of the State of Safety (SoS) for a damaged electric vehicle (EV). This paper introduces a method for rapidly and precisely assessing the SoS of lithium-ion battery packs that may have been damaged in an accident. Mean-based voltage and temperature residuals are produced for cell groups and deviations are calculated and statistically evaluated. Synthetic anomalous data is generated by injecting model-based anomalies into experimental data to simulate EV accident scenarios. The proposed post-crash safety assessment algorithm is accurate with a low false positive and false negative rates.

articleTitle: A Basic Study on Modelling and Range-Extension Control for Dual IM-PMSM Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper proposes a model-based control system to extend the range of dual-motor all-wheel-drive electric vehicles (EVs) using different electric motors (EMs). By analyzing EM, wheel, and chassis dynamics, a cost function involving driving force distribution ratio and motor current is introduced to minimize input power. An optimal driving force distribution strategy is developed to minimize energy consumption, suitable for real-time execution on conventional EV electronic control units. Computer simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of this strategy in both constant speed and acceleration/deceleration modes.

articleTitle: Improving Efficiency of Farming Tractor Implement by Electrification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to present how the Fuel Efficiency of a tractor-implement system can be increased by replacing the hydraulics of a Planter with electric machines. The analysis of the power flows of the implement based on field data is the first step to build a simulation model of the Planter, that is then connected - both mechanics and hydraulics - to the multibody model of a farming tractor. The electrification of the Planter consists of replacing the hydraulics with electric machines supplied by a generator connected to the engine shaft. The simulation results of the tractor-implement models show a significant improvement in terms of fuel consumption reduction for the electrified system compared to the baseline one.

articleTitle: Energy management system of an Electric Vehicle - IEEE VTS Challenge 2024
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: In this paper, we illustrate two families of energy management strategies for an electric vehicle equipped with an internal permanent magnet motor supplied by a battery and a supercapacitor (SC). The strategies aim to minimize the size and energy consumption of the storage system, as well as the losses and costs associated with power electronics converters. Both strategies share the same motor control approach, designed to maximize torque per Ampere, thereby reducing the required current to maintain a specified speed profile. In terms of current distribution between battery and SC, the first strategy (Spref) splits current into low-frequency components to the battery and high frequencies to the SC. A PID controller which reference depends on vehicle speed prevents the SC from reaching a low charge or high charge status. Instead, the second strategy (Ploss) focuses on optimally splitting the current demand to minimize the power losses on the supply side. Again, a PID controller governs the SC voltage. The methodologies have undergone testing across various speed profiles. The results and comparison are discussed for their potential suitability for the IEEE VTS Challenge 2024.

articleTitle: Active Support Performance of Grid-connected Multi-power Conversion System Based on Grid-following/Grid-forming Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The power conversion system (PCS) serves as a crucial intermediary between energy storage system and the power grid. Presently, PCS predominantly employs two control strategies: grid-following (GFL) control and grid-forming (GFM) control. Traditional GFL converters primarily rely on phase-locked loops (PLL) to achieve synchronization with the grid, behaving as controlled current sources, which are incapable of actively supporting grid frequency and voltage. Conversely, GFM converters actively sense disturbance and possess the capability to actively support grid frequency and voltage. However, for multi-PCS grid-connected system, there remains a lack of in-depth investigation into the rational design of the configuration ratio (CR) between two types of converters. This paper investigates multi-PCS grid-connected system based on GFL/GFM control by considering different CRs. Initially, the operational principles and control strategies of multi-PCS grid-connected system are analyzed, elucidating the mathematical models of multi-PCS and their GFL/GFM controllers. Subsequently, a 6-PCSs grid-connected system is employed as an example with seven different CRs simulated in PSCAD/EMTDC, which is disturbed by load disturbance and single-phase ground fault. Finally, the simulation results are compared to obtain the optimal configuration ratio for 6-PCS grid-connected system under corresponding condition.

articleTitle: An experimental analysis of driver influence on battery electric bus energy consumption
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: With the increasing emphasis on environmental sustainability, the electrification of urban public bus fleets has gained significant attention. In this context, understanding the factors influencing the energy consumption of battery electric buses (BEBs) is crucial for optimizing their operation. This paper presents an analysis of the influence of driver behavior on BEB energy consumption based on experimental measurements. The study investigates the relationship between energy consumption, traffic conditions, and driver characteristics using data collected from an 18-day experimental campaign involving a 12 m full-electric battery bus operating on four different routes. Various parameters, including vehicle mass, driver behavior, route characteristics, and environmental conditions, are analyzed to assess their impact on BEB energy consumption. Results indicate a strong correlation between driver behavior, particularly acceleration patterns and throttle pedal utilization, and energy consumption of the electric traction motor. Overall, this study provides valuable insights into optimizing BEB operations for enhanced sustainability and performance in urban transportation systems.

articleTitle: Highly Manufacturable Edgewise Winding Design Integrating Cooling Solutions for High Power Density Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Edgewise winding is reported recently for high-performance electric machines. However, to achieve widespread uptake of electric machines, it is essential to consider the manufacturing time of the complete machine solution. For example, with different winding topologies, the cooling solutions for edgewise winding machines will be different compared to traditional round windings. This paper considers the manufacturability of edgewise windings through stator slot shape and winding cross section. A variety of cooling solutions are incorporated to increase power density, designed such that the high-quality thermal transfer pathways of edgewise windings are exploited. The contribution of the paper is the design and simulation of a manufacturable edgewise winding using finite element software for electromagnetic design and losses, as well as thermal analysis with a lumped parameter thermal network. The edgewise winding structure is developed and compared with various cooling solutions incorporated for high power density applications. The power density for the proposed, easier-to-manufacture parallel tooth edgewise winding topology is increased by 13.6% compared to the parallel slot edgewise winding with a slot opening duct cooling.

articleTitle: Switching algorithms of a CC-CV strategy for battery charging of electric vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This study examines the Constant Current-Constant Voltage (CC-CV) charging strategy for batteries of electric vehicles. The charging subsystem model and control are organised using the Energetic Macroscopic Representation formalism. The coupling of a CC control loop and a CV control loop is insured by a switching algorithm. Various algorithms are explored: a binary switching, a progressive switching and a current limitation technique. Despite its simplicity, the binary switching leads to some current peaks in the battery. The two other switching algorithms avoid this drawback. The charging time remains the same for all the switching algorithms.

articleTitle: Enhanced EMR-Based Modelling for Electric Urban Buses Performance Studies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper presents an advanced methodology focusing on Energetic Macroscopic Representation (EMR)-based modelling for accurate characterization, validation, and simulation of lithium cells in electric urban buses. Specifically tailored to the Karsan eJest minibus, this approach includes detailed cell characterization, rigorous validation processes, and comprehensive vehicle simulations. By leveraging real-world data and EMR techniques, the objective is to establish a robust framework that integrates detailed battery modelling with system-level performance analysis for precise and future aging studies. Through meticulous EMR-based modelling, validation, and vehicle simulation, this work lays a solid foundation for understanding battery dynamics and optimizing operational strategies for long-term performance and sustainability in electric urban transportation.

articleTitle: Impact of start-stop and load cycling on the lifetime of PEMFC-powered vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: In response to the urgent need to address climate change, the electrification of vehicles will have an important role in the future. In addition to electric battery vehicles, the development of vehicles incorporating PEMFC (Proton exchange membrane fuel cells) systems powered by on-board hydrogen must be included. Although hydrogen fuel cell technology has made great progress in the last twenty years, with the advent of extra-fine reinforced membranes (<15μm) the deployment of hydrogen-powered vehicles has remained constrained by the durability limitation, The aim of the research project is to determine shutdown and start-up optimal strategies for PEMFC and to optimise their functioning to increase their durability. The aim is to achieve an average degradation rate less than 10μV/h, and if possible, even 5μV/h, for an overall lifetime of between 8,000 and 12,000 h.

articleTitle: Low Voltage Battery Capacity Optimization Method for Vehicles by Connecting Supercapacitor in Series
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Most electrical vehicles and internal combustion engine vehicles are implementing lithium-ion batteries as one of low voltage power source for 12V/48V loads, cooperating with vehicle HV/LV DCDC. Energy demands are not the dominant factor for determining battery capacity thanks to high energy density of lithium-ion battery. However, power demands with specified voltage limit will lead to a large battery capacity, especially when battery requires to run under cold environments. Implementing large battery capacity means bigger battery pack dimensions, heavier weight, and higher cost which will have an influence on vehicle’s overall performance and sales. Thus, OEMs consider battery capacity as a key factor for selecting low voltage batter supplier during sourcing. This paper introduces a method where supercapacitor could be integrated into the battery pack and could be controlled to be connected with lithium-ion battery module in series according to detected profile by BMS or control signals from vehicle, which could solve limited power problems of lithium-ion battery and will drive a small battery size with lower overall cost of battery pack. Related simulations result will also be covered in this paper to prove the feasibility of above concept. Furthermore, this technology could also be applied on similar energy storage situation, including energy storage station and so forth.

articleTitle: Geometric Scaling Laws for Axial Flux Permanent Magnet Motors in In-Wheel Powertrain Topologies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: In this paper, we present geometric scaling models for axial flux motors (AFMs) to be used for in-wheel powertrain design optimization purposes. We first present a vehicle and powertrain model, with emphasis on the electric motor model. We construct the latter by formulating the analytical scaling laws for AFMs, based on the scaling concept of RFMs from the literature, specifically deriving the model of the main loss component in electric motors: the copper losses. We further present separate scaling models of motor parameters, losses and thermal models, as well as the torque limits and cost, as a function of the design variables. Second, we validate these scaling laws with several experiments leveraging high-fidelity finite-element simulations. Finally, we define an optimization problem that minimizes the energy consumption over a drive cycle, optimizing the motor size and transmission ratio for a wide range of electric vehicle powertrain topologies. In our study, we observe that the all-wheel drive topology equipped with in-wheel AFMs is the most efficient, but also generates the highest material cost.

articleTitle: Flexible Automotive Power Management: Formalization of an Auction-based Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The electrification of former mechanical components and the expansion of infotainment systems lead to an increasing automotive power network (APN) in terms of components and power consumption. Additionally, customers desire a flexible hardware composition. As a consequence, automotive power management has to ensure power balancing for volatile generation and demand and to support the integration of new hardware during development, vehicle configuration, and even after production. In this paper, we propose an adapted management architecture, formalize an auction framework for automotive power management of APNs with multiple voltage levels, and show respective simulation results.

articleTitle: Robust Wheel Speed Control of Electric Vehicles with Respect to Backlash and Dead-time in Powertrains
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The primary advantage of electric vehicles (EVs) lies in their rapid and precise torque generation. Consequently, the research and development of traction control systems that ensure safety, stability, and reliability in EVs are becoming increasingly popular. In this paper, an analysis of the wheel-speed control of an EV under various operating conditions is presented. A double-loop cascade disturbance observer (DOB) was designed to estimate the wheel speed from the estimation of the total disturbance acting on the vehicle. The influence of gear backlash, torque delay, air drag, and road inclination were analyzed to investigate the effectiveness of the control system. The preliminary Matlab simulation analysis demonstrated that the DOB-based control design was effective and robust to the effects of external disturbances.

articleTitle: SOH Estimation Algorithm and Hardware Platform for Lithium-ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper presents a state-of-health (SOH) estimation algorithm and hardware platform for lithium-ion batteries. Based on features obtained from the battery's electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), an artificial neural network (ANN)-based SOH algorithm is developed. EIS measurements collected at different aging levels are utilized to train and test the SOH estimation algorithm. The minimum impedance magnitude and the impedance magnitude at zero phase show correlations with the battery SOH level and can be utilized to indicate the SOH value. The SOH estimation algorithm performance is evaluated, and the performance evaluation results indicate that the SOH estimation algorithm can be utilized to estimate the SOH.

articleTitle: A 3D Multiphysics Study of Different Channel Designs Of PEM Electrolyzer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The production of hydrogen through an electrolysis cell powered by green energy has garnered attention during the last decades. This study investigates the uniformity of distribution of variables in proton exchange membrane electrolysis cells (PEMEC), including current density, pressure, velocity, and molar fraction of species. Different channel shapes are considered in the 3D model created within COMSOL Multiphysics, considering multiphysics behaviors like mass transfer, phase transfer in porous media, fluid dynamics, and electrochemical reaction kinetics. Based on the obtained results, a particular multichannel configuration performs better than other configurations due to the fact that it lowers both singular and linear losses and increases distribution uniformity.

articleTitle: Impact of electric vehicle charging on the power grid: a simulation framework for the validation of new services
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: In order to minimize the impact of electric vehicle (EV) charging on the electric grid, it is essential to implement new software-based services such as smart charging and demand response. This paper introduces a simulation framework to evaluate and validate these new services, focusing on two levels of impact: charging scheduling at a macroscopic level and delving into the specific actions of the charging stations. This paper concentrates on the latter and proposes a Hardware in the Loop (HIL) model that integrates three components: the information technology (IT) aspect, the power grid aspect and the behavior of the battery charger subsystem. It presents an original methodology and validates it with various usage scenarios highlighting the effects of EV charging on grid stability.

articleTitle: Method for defining Hybrid Powertrain Architectures for Off-Highway Vehicles based on Power Flow Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper presents a method for designing hybrid electric powertrain architectures for off-highway vehicles, based on the analysis of the power flows of the system during operation. For this purpose the conventional powertrain layout is first considered with its main components and their power absorption. The approach is based on efficiency maps or power losses of each component. Then, the duty cycle of such vehicles must be analyzed, defining the operation points for different type of work and then the working points of the vehicle components. After collecting insights from this analysis, many hybrid electric architectures can be made up, each one designed to improve the efficiency of the vehicles for a set of operating point conditions.

articleTitle: Tutorials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)

articleTitle: IEEE VTS Motor Vehicle Challenge 2025 – Energy Management and Control of a Marine Electric Propulsion System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The topic proposed for the IEEE VTS Motor Vehicle Challenge 2025 (MVC 2025) consists of developing an energy management strategy for a marine Electric Propulsion System (EPS). The key component of the proposed EPS is a Dual Three-Phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine (DTPPMSM), whose windings are supplied by a Battery Pack (BP) and a Supercapacitor Module (SM) through appropriate DC/DC and DC/AC converters. The DTP-PMSM shaft is connected to a marine propeller, which is devoted to develop the thrust force needed to move the vessel. The MVC 2025 participants should propose an energy management strategy that splits the DTPPMSM power demand among its two windings, each of which is supplied by a different energy storage unit, by minimizing a given cost function.

articleTitle: A Modified Deadbeat Predictive Current Control with Improved Dynamic Performance under Insufficient Voltage Margin for IPMSM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper proposes a modified deadbeat predictive current control (DPCC) method with improved dynamic performance under insufficient voltage margin conditions for interior permanent magnet synchronous motors (IPMSMs). When command currents cannot be tracked within two control periods due to voltage limitations, the proposed method extends the prediction horizon to encompass the entire dynamic process and derives the control equations based on an exact discretized motor model. Additionally, the motor model is further incrementalized to eliminate the need for rotor flux linkage. Simulation results demonstrate that the dynamic performance of both current and torque can be improved by the proposed method compared to the conventional minimum-phase-error voltage limiting strategy.

articleTitle: Vehicle Convoy Control for Minimizing Total CO2 Emissions Considering Social Acceptability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel vehicle convoy control system that aims to contribute to carbon neutrality while ensuring social acceptance. One of the challenges faced in achieving energy reduction arises from the significant deviation of automated driving and manual driving from conventional driving maneuvers, which can cause discomfort. To address this challenge, we have improved the previously proposed control strategy, which is both simple and effective in reducing CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions from vehicle convoys, in order to minimize discomfort in driving behavior. Additionally, we conducted an effect verification in a realistic environment by classifying two traffic light sequences on an existing route. The results show a reduction of up to 14% in CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions for battery electric vehicles when the controlled vehicle and its following vehicles pass through intersections.

articleTitle: The Impact of Dynamic Deceleration Limit on Optimal Speed Planning for Fuel Cell Hybrid Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Speed profiles and energy management strategy (EMS) significantly influence the energy efficiency of fuel cell hybrid electric vehicles (FCHEVs). Sequential optimization of speed planning and EMS in two layers could be beneficial over co-optimization in terms of computational burden and speed. Traditionally, speed planning is constrained by the electric motor’s capabilities, alongside minimum deceleration rates, to ensure safe and realistic vehicle maneuvers. However, these constraints typically overlook the battery and power electronics’ capacity to store regenerative power, with power allocation issues being addressed only in the subsequent layer. In response, a new dynamic deceleration rate that incorporates the regenerative capacity limits directly into the speed planning layer has been introduced in this study. The energy efficiency of optimal speed profiles generated using this novel approach is compared with conventional speed profiles under winter conditions, demonstrating enhanced performance and energy recovery.

articleTitle: The impact of stack allocation on the performance of a hybrid multi-stack fuel cell system
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Multi-stack fuel cell systems (MFCSs), composed of multiple low-power fuel cells operating independently, offer increased power range, reliability, space flexibility, and modularity, making them ideal for heavy-duty applications. The performance of MFCSs is influenced by both the number and combinations of stacks that are used to construct the system. This paper examines the impact of these factors on the operational costs of fuel cell systems (FCS), encompassing hydrogen consumption and stack degradation costs. Three case studies are investigated, and in each case, the best allocation scheme is introduced based on the value of the objective function. Sequential quadratic programming (SQP) is selected to perform energy management among power sources. Also, the results demonstrate that increasing the number of stacks from two to three resulted in a 6.33% reduction in operational costs, while further augmenting the number of stacks from three to four notably decreased expenses by approximately 14.87%.

articleTitle: Model-Predictive Direct Flux Vector Control for Synchronous Reluctance Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This paper proposes a model-predictive direct flux vector control (MPDFVC) for synchronous reluctance (SynRel) machines. Compared with the widely adopted vector control based in rotor synchronous rotating coordinate system, the proposed control strategy is built upon control variables in stator flux-oriented frame, i.e., stator flux and torque-producing current. The integration of direct flux control with predictive control aims to enhance dynamic performance and mitigate the cross-coupling effects of SynRel machines by utilizing the inherent bandwidth advantages of predictive control. Key features of the proposed controller include torque and flux reference tracking terms, as well as a soft constraint on switching effort to reduce switching frequency and current distortions. Validation through simulation and experimental tests demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed approach, showing fast dynamic response, reduced overshoots and undershoots of stator current, and minimized cross-coupling between state variables.

Author Keywords: Finite Control Set Model Predictive Control

articleTitle: A CHB grid⁃forming Energy Storage Control Strategy Considering SOC Balance in Unbalanced Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: A cascaded H-bridge(CHB) grid⁃forming energy storage control strategy considering the state of charge (SOC) balance in unbalanced grid is presented. Utilizing voltage-type virtual synchronous generator (VSG) control enables grid-forming energy storage to address issues arising from the characteristics of renewable energy sources, such as low inertia and underdamping, which result in insufficient voltage support and lower power supply reliability. Establishing a mathematical model of the VSG, the synthesized three-phase voltage serves as the positive-sequence voltage command signal for the voltage-current loop. Addressing SOC issues present in VSG based on CHB in unbalanced grids, a SOC-balancing control method based on negative-sequence voltage closed-loop is proposed, with the injected negative-sequence voltage serving as the instruction signal. The stability of the VSG is assessed through root locus analysis, followed by the design of critical parameters. Finally, simulation analysis is conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed CHB grid⁃forming energy storage control strategy considering SOC-balancing in unbalanced grid.

articleTitle: Hysteresis in Sodium-ion Batteries: Temperature and Relaxation Time Effects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This study investigates the impact of temperature and relaxation time on sodium-ion battery hysteresis. To achieve the latter, accurate characterization of the relationship between open-circuit voltage and state-of-charge was implemented. This relationship was further modeled using the MATLAB curve fitting toolbox keeping the root mean squared error below 5%. The experimental results reveal significant hysteresis levels, particularly at low state-of-charge values, reaching a maximum of 0.2252V. In addition, hysteresis diminishes with increasing temperature and relaxation time. These results underscore the importance of accounting for hysteresis and its variations when accurately estimating state-of-charge and optimizing battery performance.

articleTitle: HiL Demonstration of Online Battery Capacity and Impedance Estimation with Minimal a Priori Parametrization Effort
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Uncertainty in the aging of batteries in battery electric vehicles impacts both the daily driving range as well as the expected economic lifetime. This paper presents a method to determine online the capacity and internal resistance of a battery cell based on real-world data. The method, based on a Joint Extended Kalman Filter combined with Recursive Least Squares, is computationally efficient and does not a priori require a fully characterized cell model. Offline simulation of the algorithm on data from differently aged cells shows convergence of the algorithm and indicates that capacity and resistance follow the expected trends. Furthermore, the algorithm is tested online on a Hardware-in-the-Loop setup to demonstrate real-time parameter updates in a realistic driving scenario.

articleTitle: Efficient Energy and Loss Management Control Strategy for a Hybrid e-Racing Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This work describes the design and control strategy of an electric vehicle equipped with a battery pack and a supercapacitor, which scored second place in the eighth edition of the IEEE VTS Motor Vehicles challenge. Other than selecting the number of SiC-MOSFET modules to be connected in parallel for each converter leg in the vehicle, challenge contenders had to develop a strategy that regulates the current flowing through the main drive inverter and distributes the power request between the battery and the supercapacitor to optimize specific performance metrics. Simulation results in several driving cycles demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed solution.

articleTitle: Energetic Macroscopic Representation of a Partial Power Converter based Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle is one of the solutions envisaged reducing greenhouse gas emissions in the transportation sector. Generally, a fuel cell is connected to a second energy source, such as a battery. The connection is realized using an interleaved boost converter. In recent years, a new converter candidate has emerged in the literature: the partial power converter. This converter is intended to connect the fuel cell to the other parts of the vehicle instead of the classical boost converter. Simulations are needed to assess the energetic performance of the partial power converter integrated to the vehicle. A comparison with the boost converter is performed with the same constant efficiency. This study demonstrates a theoretical reduction of 4% of the losses to the advantage of the partial power converter.

articleTitle: Simulation-Based Analysis of Battery Electric Vehicles Driving Range in Response to Thermal Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This study introduces a development process of a simulation framework to analyze the driving range for battery electric vehicles (BEVs) under different thermal conditions, utilizing real-world test data for validation. The framework assesses BEVs' range and energy efficiency at ambient and cold temperatures by incorporating battery parameters, motor efficiency maps, and estimates of heating power. The results closely align with real-world test results, with simulation errors within acceptable limits for over 90% of vehicles at ambient temperatures and over 80% at cold temperatures. This accuracy supports the Korean certification organization in efficiently reviewing and screening BEVs for the market.

articleTitle: Detailed simulation and energy management of the trains in the new proposed Green Line in Jerusalem
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: We have modelled in great detail the track and the train for the already under construction green line in the light rail system in the Jerusalem LRT Network (J-Net) in Israel. We have included many technical and operational constraints, while also rigorously formulating a mathematical optimization problem describing the operation of the railway. Our model can include several objective functions, considering different driving strategies as well as cost or time minimization. The results obtained are illustrative and can inform railway operators when making important operational and strategic decisions.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Pole-Changing Vernier Memory Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The design and analysis of a Pole-Changing Vernier Memory Machine (PCVMM) for electric vehicles is presented in this paper. This configuration aims to extend the high-efficiency constant power region by exploiting both the PC technique and the magnetic gear effect. As a result, PCVMM can work at two different synchronous speeds but at the same rated supply frequency, operating as either a Vernier machine and or a traditional Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine (PMSM). Consequently, a wide speed range is achieved without resorting to bulky and inefficient mechanical gear transmission systems and expensive high-performance power electronic converters. The proposed PCVMM is designed by finite element analyses and compared with a traditional PMSM of the same size in order to confirm and validate the design choices.

articleTitle: Assessment of Torque Vectoring Controllers Performance through Subjective-Objective Ratings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: With the increasing demand for enhanced vehicle performance and handling dynamics, torque vectoring has emerged as a fundamental technology in modern automotive engineering. Consequently, several control logics have been designed through the years and their performance has been assessed through objective metrics quantifying how the controlled vehicle is able to track a reference for its lateral dynamics. Nevertheless, this evaluation approach is rather limited because it is not accounting for the feedback from an actual driver. Thus, this paper addresses this critical gap in the evaluation of torque vectoring controllers by including drivers’ subjective evaluations through Driver-in-the-Loop simulations. Indeed, the research comprehensively analyzes both objective metrics and subjective driver assessments, examining the impact of different torque vectoring control strategies on vehicle dynamics. By correlating quantitative metrics with human perception, this integrated approach enhances the understanding of torque vectoring control strategies' effectiveness and their real-world implications on driver satisfaction.

articleTitle: Gain Scheduled Control with Youla Interpolation Conditions: A Design Example
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: A new Linear Parameter Varying dynamic output feedback controller design technique is presented based on the Youla-Kucera Interpolation Conditions. The original method, used for Linear Time Invariant systems, is extended to Linear Parameter Varying systems. The application of this technique is demonstrated and validated with the design of a path-tracking controller for an Automated Driving System. The validation uses a CarSim-Simulink co-simulation that incorporates two different environment models. Simulation results for two aggressive maneuvers show that the resulting controller performs well in normal and low-friction environments with severe external disturbances.

articleTitle: Impact of Optimal Fuel Cell Management System on Fuel Cell Hybrid Electric Vehicle Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Fuel cell hybrid electric vehicles (FCHEVs) play an important role in driving the transition towards more environment-friendly transportation and electric mobility. Their powertrain efficiency hinges on the effective distribution of power demands between the fuel cell (FC) and the battery, facilitated by an Energy Management System (EMS). In the literature, diverse strategies are utilized to handle the power allocation within the FCHEV. Unlike existing work, this paper breaks new ground by incorporating a Fuel Cell Management System (FCMS) into the EMS. This FCMS improves FC performance by simultaneously monitoring FC operational conditions: temperature and oxygen excess ratio. The proposed optimal FCMS is combined with the Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) EMS and simulated across urban, suburban, and highway driving scenarios. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, by achieving up to 4% enhancement in the overall efficiency.

articleTitle: Implementing Neural Networks in Model Predictive Controller for Battery Thermal Management System of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Interest in electric vehicles is rapidly increasing as the environmental regulations on internal combustion engine vehicles become more stringent. However, electric vehicles still have disadvantages in driving range and safety compared to internal combustion engine vehicles. The driving range and safety of electric vehicles are closely related to battery temperature. Therefore, a battery thermal management system is necessary for electric vehicles to maintain the battery temperature within optimal operating range. However, the battery thermal management system consumes considerable energy during operation. Consequently, this paper presents model predictive controller design for battery thermal management system of electric vehicles which minimizes the energy consumption while maintaining the battery temperature in proper operating range. Additionally, an artificial neural network-based control model of battery thermal management system has been developed for reducing computational load and enhance model accuracy.

articleTitle: Optimal thermal management on the storage vessle for cryogenic hydrogen-powered hybrid train
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The paper proposes an optimal thermal management for subcooled liquid hydrogen system for hybrid hydrogen-powered train. A hybrid train simulator, combined with the cryogenic hydrogen defuelling model, is developed to predict the real-time hydrogen thermodynamic state inside the storage tank for the whole journey. Three strategies are carefully discussed for the corresponding stages of cryogenic hydrogen defueling process. The result shows different types of thermal management schemes need to be adopted to stabilise hydrogen output flow and keep the hydrogen state within safety standards while train operation.

articleTitle: Current Control Schemes for Grid Following Inverter-based Onshore Electrified Ship
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: In the context of environmental conservation and sustainable development goals, the shipping industry is transitioning towards renewable energy sources instead of fossil fuels. Equipping ships with batteries and connecting them to the onshore grid through inverter-based resources (IBR) offers numerous benefits, such as reducing greenhouse gas emissions and optimizing energy use. However, ensuring the quality and stability of the electrical current when connected to the grid presents significant challenges. This paper compares three electrical current control methods: inverter-side control, grid-side cascade control, and grid-side single control, to enhance the quality and stability of the electrical current from ship batteries when connected to the onshore grid (grid-following inverter) under both strong and weak grid scenarios. The model, developed through simulation using the Energetic Macroscopic Representation (EMR) method, provides valuable insights. The results of this study will aid in selecting appropriate control methods for ports, promoting the widespread adoption of sustainable practices in the shipping industry.

articleTitle: Dynamic Simulation Model of an inWheel IPT System based on Experimental Characterization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: Inductive Power Transfer (IPT) is a promising technology with the potential to revolutionise various sectors, including transportation, offering numerous advantages. Further research is essential to understand its behaviour and optimize efficiency under varied conditions, including the study of in-wheel IPT (inWIPT) technology. This system uses the wheel to transfer energy to the vehicle, maintaining a consistent air gap regardless of the vehicle type. This work presents a simulation model of inWIPT system developed for the dynamic charging scenario and an assessment is made to understand its behaviour. Magnetic Couplers (MC)s are characterized for self/mutual inductances used for simulations, considering wheel movement, rotation, lateral displacements, and airgap. A prototype is built to validate the MCs behavioural analysis and the simulation model under different conditions.

articleTitle: High Pole Number Outer-Rotor SPM Machine for Sustainable 150kW High-Speed EV Traction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: The ambitious roadmaps of electric vehicle (EV) powertrains are pushing traction motors to achieve step-change performance improvements in power density, efficiency, and cost by 2035. Limited by technology bricks such as materials, manufacturing and thermal management, the widely adopted interior permanent magnet (IPM) machine solutions are reaching their performance boundaries in multi-physics domains. This digest will introduce a feasibility study of outer rotor surface mounted PM (OR-SPM) motor against these leading performance KPIs for high speed EV traction. Through comparison with state of the art interior PM (IPM) machine solutions under the same torque-speed requirements, active material properties as well as converter specifications, it is found that an OR-SPM motor with high pole number is a promising topology from sustainability perspective. Global optimisation of a down-sifted 72-slot, 24-pole OR-SPM motor is then conducted based on finite element tools. It is revealed that compared with a benchmark 150kW IPM motor, >20% magnet usage reduction can be achieved. Meanwhile, the study also identifies the challenge in the relatively low partial load efficiency of the optimised design. Methods to improve the efficiency based on core material selection are then investigated. It is found that for the proposed OR-SPM solution, amorphous steel with ultra-low iron loss behaviour is a promising candidate material for significant efficiency improvement.

articleTitle: Methodology for characterizing the aging of a PEMFC based on a real-life usage database
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Vehicle Power and Propulsion Conference (VPPC)
abstract: This article proposes a methodology to estimate the aging of a PEMFC with the associated weight of degradation mechanisms.
